Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming with iOS 27, the Passwords app is set to receive a particularly powerful new capability: automatically changing your passwords for you.

iOS 27's Passwords app, powered by Apple Intelligence, can fix compromised login credentials on your behalf

The new generation of Apple Intelligence is at the core of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One of the powerful new AI features is tied to the Apple Passwords app.

The Passwords app, launched two years ago, serves as a dedicated hub for managing login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always flagged passwords in your vault that have issues. For example, if your password appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

But until now, you've always had to manually fix those problematic login credentials yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says its new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you in many situations. According to its website:

With this feature, you can ensure your credentials are always secure and use strong passwords, while minimising the time and hassle required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will roll out to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut with iOS 27.0, but its rollout in the beta has been unstable, so it may end up arriving in iOS 27.1 instead.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Let us know in the comments.
